title: Lesson 1: Set

exercises.text: When we group a collection of objects together, such as all school supplies in a backpack, we form a __________.
Every single item inside a collection is called an __________ of that group.
If the number 3 is part of group A, we write 3 ∈ A and say that 3 __________ group A.
Since 10 is not inside the group of single-digit numbers, we say that 10 __________ that specific collection.
An __________ is a collection that contains absolutely no items or members in it.
The __________ consists of all counting numbers starting from zero: 0, 1, 2, 3,...

title: Lesson 2: Writing natural numbers

exercises.text: In the number 458, the number 8 is in the __________, meaning it represents 8 units.
The number 10 is the smallest two-digit __________ used for counting objects in everyday life.
To write the number 15 using ancient symbols, we use the __________ XV.
A single __________ like 7 can be used to form larger numbers.
In the standard base-10 __________, the position of each number determines its overall value.
In the number 732, the digit 3 is located in the __________, which represents 3 groups of ten.
Each position of a digit in a multi-digit number has a specific __________ that helps us read its exact magnitude.
In the number 946, the digit 9 sits in the __________ and has a value of 900.

title: Lesson 3: Order in the set of natural numbers

exercises.text: On the number line starting from origin O, the point representing a number a lies at a distance equal to a units from O. When we want to evaluate two distinct natural numbers to see which one is smaller, we can ___________ them.
On a horizontal number line, the point representing the smaller number is located to the left, which means it is ___________ the larger number.
Conversely, the point representing the larger number is located to the right, meaning it is ___________ the smaller number.
In mathematics, when we consider values that can be smaller or match another quantity, we use the relation of being ___________.
Similarly, the relation of being ___________ covers cases where a value is greater than or equal to another.
If a ∈ ℕ, then a is called the ___________ of a + 1.
On the other hand, a + 1 is called the ___________ of a.

title: Lesson 4: Addition and subtraction of natural numbers

exercises.text: The operation of combining numbers together to find a total is called ___________.
In an addition expression, each of the numbers being added (such as 25 and 11) is called an ___________.
The result of an addition operation (such as 36) is called the ___________.
The operation of taking one number away from another is called ___________.
The result of a subtraction operation (such as 25) is called the ___________.
The ___________ allows us to change the order of addends in a sum without changing the final result.
The ___________ allows us to group addends differently when calculating a sum.
The property where adding 0 to any number leaves the number unchanged is known as ___________.

title: Lesson 5: Multiplication and division of natural numbers

exercises.text: To quickly calculate the total number of items arranged in rows and columns (e.g., finding the area or total items), we use the operation of ___________.
In the expression 25 × 2 = 50, the numbers 25 and 2 play the role of a ___________, while 50 is called the ___________.
When applying the ___________, we can change the order or group numbers differently when multiplying multiple terms together without altering the final outcome.
To calculate 12 × (10 + 3) efficiently by expanding it as (12 × 10) + (12 × 3), we rely on the ___________.
If we have 36 candies to share equally among 12 friends, we use ___________ to find out how many each person gets, which gives a ___________ of 3.
In a standard division setup like 36 ÷ 12 = 3, the number 36 being shared is the ___________, and 12 is the ___________.
When a natural number can be divided by another with no left-over amount, we say that the first number is ___________ by the second.
If we distribute 36 items among 15 people and find that some are left over, we are performing a ___________.
In the division statement 36 ÷ 15 = 2 (remainder 6), the amount left over (6) is specifically called the ___________, and it must always be strictly less than the divisor.

title: Lesson 6: Powers with natural-number exponents
wordBank: Multiplying powers with the same base
Dividing powers with the same base

exercises.text: Instead of writing a long multiplication like 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 3, we use a shorthand notation called a ___________, written as 3⁵.
In the expression 3⁵, the repeated factor 3 is the ___________, while 5 is the ___________, which tells us how many times 3 is multiplied by itself.
When a number is raised to the second power, such as 10² = 10 × 10, we call this operation finding the ___________ of 10.
Similarly, raising a number to the third power, like 4³ = 4 × 4 × 4, is known as finding its ___________.
To simplify 5³ × 5² into 5³⁺² = 5⁵, we apply the rule for ___________ by keeping the base and adding the exponents.
answers: Multiplying powers with the same base

exercises.text: When simplifying 5³ ÷ 5² into 5³⁻² = 5¹ (for a ≠ 0 and m ≥ n), we use the rule for ___________, which requires subtracting the exponents.
answers: Dividing powers with the same base

exercises.text: If you encounter an expression like (2 × 5)³ and rewrite it as 2³ × 5³, you are applying the ___________ rule.
To simplify a nested exponential expression such as (5²)³ into 5²×³ = 5⁶, you multiply the exponents using the ___________ rule.

title: Lesson 7: Order of operations

exercises.text: Look at the mathematical phrase 2x + 1. Because it combines numbers, operations, and a variable without an equals sign, we call it an algebraic ___________.
If we substitute x = 2 into 2x + 1 and compute 2 × 2 + 1 = 5, the final result 5 is called the ___________ when x = 2.
To solve 3² - 5[3(4 - 1) - 8] without making mistakes, we must first simplify the inner grouping symbols, known as ___________, before moving to the outer ones.

Why does 12 + 3 × 2⁵ ÷ 4 - 3 equal 33 instead of a different number? Because we strictly follow the ___________: calculating the power 2⁵ first, then multiplying and dividing, and finally adding and subtracting.

title: Lesson 8: Divisibility relations and properties

exercises.text: When we write a = kb (with k ∈ ℕ), we state that a is ___________ b (denoted as b | a).
If 12 is divisible by 4, then 4 is called a ___________ of 12, and conversely, 12 is called a ___________ of 4.
If you divide 10 by 3, you get a remainder, which means 10 is ___________ by 3.
When examining whether the sum 15 + 12 is divisible by 3, we use the ___________, knowing that since both 15 and 12 are divisible by 3, their sum is also divisible by 3.
On the other hand, if we check the sum 15 + 13 with respect to 3, since 15 is divisible by 3 but 13 is not, the sum (15+13) is ___________ by 3.

title: Lesson 9: Divisibility rules

exercises.text: When checking whether a large number can divide evenly by 2 or 5 without doing long division, we apply a specific ___________ to find out quickly.
To test if a number is divisible by 2 (ending in 0,2,4,6,8) or by 5 (ending in 0 or 5), we only need to inspect its ___________.
Unlike numbers divisible by 2 or 5, checking whether a number is divisible by 3 or 9 requires us to calculate the ___________ of all its digits.

title: Lesson 10: Prime numbers

exercises.text: When checking the number 7, we find it is only divisible by 1 and itself, so it is classified as a ___________.
Unlike 7, the number 12 has multiple divisors (1,2,3,4,6,12), which makes it a ___________.
When you break down a natural number like 60 into a product of prime numbers (2 × 2 × 3 × 5), this process is called performing a ___________.
To find the prime factors of 60 visually by branching it down into smaller factors step-by-step like a plant, students often use a diagram known as a ___________.
Alternatively, if you prefer a vertical computation layout where you divide sequentially by ascending prime numbers (60 divided by 2, then 2, then 3, then 5), you are using the ___________.

title: Lesson 11: Common divisors. Greatest common divisor

exercises.text: When finding the numbers that can divide both 12 and 18 evenly, any number belonging to both lists is called a ___________ of the two numbers.
To find the largest number that divides both 12 and 18 (which is 6), we look for their ___________.
Instead of listing all divisors by hand, we can find the GCD quickly for large numbers by successive division using the ___________ or by analyzing prime factors.
If two numbers have a GCD equal to 1 (such as 8 and 9), we say they are ___________ to each other.
When simplifying a fraction like 12/18 down to 2/3 by dividing the numerator and denominator by their GCD (6), the resulting fraction is written in its ___________.

title: Lesson 12: Common multiples. Least common multiple

exercises.text: When listing the multiples of 4 and 6, any number that appears in both lists (such as 12, 24,...) is called a ___________ of those numbers.
To find the smallest non-zero number that both 4 and 6 can divide into (which is 12), we determine their ___________.
When adding two fractions with different denominators like 1/4 and 1/6, a crucial step is ___________ by using the LCM of the denominators as the new shared bottom number.

title: Lesson 13: The set of integers

exercises.text: When describing opposite real-life quantities like a temperature of 5°C above zero versus 5°C below zero, we use positive numbers and a ___________ such as -5.
The set Z containing zero, all natural numbers, and their opposites is known as the set of numbers called ___________.
Natural numbers like 1, 2, 3,... are specifically referred to as ___________.
To visualize these numbers graphically, we draw a horizontal ___________ where every point corresponds to a specific number value.
The fixed starting point 0 marked on this line is called the ___________.
Moving to the right from 0 points toward the ___________, while moving to the left points toward the ___________ where negative numbers are located.

title: Lesson 14: Addition and subtraction of integers
wordBank: Adding integers with the same sign

exercises.text: When evaluating two numbers like 5 and -5, each of them is referred to as the ___________ of the other, and their sum always equals 0.
To calculate (-3) + (-5), we apply the rule for ___________ by adding their natural numbers together and placing a minus sign in front, resulting in -8.
answers: Adding integers with the same sign

exercises.text: When combining two values with different signs like 5 + (-3), we use the rule for ___________, finding the difference between their absolute values and keeping the sign of the larger number.
To solve a calculation like 5 - (-3), we convert it into an equivalent addition problem using the rule for ___________, which rewrites it as 5 + 3.
When adding multiple integers, switching the order of numbers such that a+b=b+a demonstrates the ___________.
Similarly, grouping terms differently in a sum such that a+(b+c)=(a+b)+c relies on the ___________.

title: Lesson 15: Rules of brackets / sign rules

exercises.text: To simplify a long algebraic sum like 15-(5-8)+(-3), we apply the ___________ to decide whether the signs inside should stay the same or flip.
When we rewrite 15-(5-8) as 15-5+8 because there is a minus sign in front, we are performing the step of ___________.

By arbitrarily rearranging the terms along with their signs and grouping convenient numbers together, such as turning 15-5+8-3 into (15-5)+(8-3), we are ___________ to calculate its value much faster.

title: Lesson 16: Multiplication of integers
wordBank: Multiplying integers with the same sign
Distributive property of multiplication over addition

exercises.text: When calculating (-4) × (-5) = 20, we apply the rule for ___________, which always yields a positive product.
answers: Multiplying integers with the same sign

exercises.text: Conversely, to evaluate 4 × (-5) = -20, we follow the rule for ___________ by multiplying their natural parts and placing a minus sign in front.
To quickly compute (-25) × 17 × (-4), we first swap the positions of 17 and (-4) using the ___________.
Next, we group (-25) and (-4) together inside brackets as [(-25) × (-4)] × 17 to get 100 × 17 by applying the ___________.
When factoring out a common term to simplify (-7) × 38 + (-7) × 62 into (-7) × (38 + 62), we rely on the ___________.
answers: Distributive property of multiplication over addition

title: Lesson 17: Divisibility, factors and multiples of an integer

exercises.text: Because we can find an integer q = -4 such that -12 = 3 × (-4), the operation (-12) ÷ 3 = -4 is called an ___________ (denoted as -12 ÷ 3).

When evaluating (-15) ÷ (-5) = 3 versus (-15) ÷ 5 = -3, we determine the ___________ by checking whether the two integers share the same sign (giving a positive result) or have different signs (giving a negative result).
Since -12 is divisible by 3, the number 3—along with its opposite, -3—is considered a ___________ of -12.
Conversely, because -12 can be divided evenly by 3, both -12 and its opposite 12 belong to the set of every ___________ of 3.

title: Lesson 18: Equilateral triangle, square, regular hexagon

exercises.text: A standard warning traffic sign shaped like a three-sided polygon with all three edges of equal length is an example of an ___________.
When measuring the corner opening of a chessboard tile, you find that every ___________ is equal to 90°, which confirms the tile is shaped like a ___________.
Bees build their honeycombs using cells shaped like a ___________, a six-sided figure where each ___________ has the exact same length and each corner measures 120°.
When using a compass and ruler to construct triangle ABC, the sharp corner point A where two edges meet is called a ___________.
If you draw a straight line connecting two opposite corners of a chessboard tile (such as A and C in ABCD), you create a ___________, and both of these lines in the shape are equal in length.

title: Lesson 19: Rectangles, rhombuses, parallelograms and isosceles trapezoids

exercises.text: A standard A4 sheet of paper or a smartphone screen has four 90° corners and equal diagonals, which makes it a ___________.
When you measure the top edge of a classroom door and find it matches the exact length of the bottom edge, you are comparing an ___________ pair.
A traditional diamond-shaped kite with four equal edges and two diagonals intersecting at a right angle (90°) is a classic example of a ___________.

If you gently push the top of a rectangular wooden frame sideways so its corners tilt away from 90° while its opposite edges stay parallel and equal in length, the frame transforms into a ___________.
A symmetrical wooden roof beam or a popcorn bucket with a wider top base than its parallel bottom base is shaped like an ___________.
In that symmetrical bucket shape, the two slanted non-parallel edges on the left and right are equal in length, and each one is called a ___________.

title: Lesson 20: Perimeter and area of quadrilaterals

exercises.text: Squares, rectangles, trapezoids, parallelograms, and rhombuses all share a common feature: they are closed four-sided polygons, which puts them in the family of shapes known as a ___________.
If you want to build a wooden fence completely around a rectangular garden with sides a and b, you need to calculate the total boundary length using the ___________ formula P = 2(a + b).
To buy enough grass turf to cover the entire surface inside a diamond-shaped (rhombus) courtyard with diagonals a and b, you must find its total ___________ using the formula S = ab/2.

title: Lesson 21: Line / axial symmetry

exercises.text: If you fold a picture of a butterfly right down its center line and find that both sides match up completely, the butterfly is an example of an ___________.
The imaginary straight line running down the middle of a regular hexagon or an isosceles trapezoid that lets you fold the shape into two identical parts is called the ___________.
When performing a paper-folding test along this folding line, the two halves created on either side must ___________ each other perfectly.
These two folded parts are referred to as ___________ because they have the exact same shape and size.
If an asymmetric leaf or an irregular shape cannot be folded along any line to make its sides match up, we describe its structure as ___________.
When checking the symmetry of a line segment AB drawn on grid paper, the folding line always passes perpendicularly through the exact ___________ of that segment.

title: Lesson 22: Central symmetry

exercises.text: If you pin a decorative four-petal flower pattern at a fixed point O and rotate it half a turn (180°) so that it matches its original position, the pattern is called a ___________.
___________ is a geometric property found in many pinwheels and playing cards, where turning the object upside down leaves its appearance unchanged.
When spinning a round bicycle wheel, its ___________ acts as the exact turning point, making every ___________ a symmetric shape.
To find the turning point of a ___________ (like an A4 sheet of paper) or a ___________ (like a chessboard tile), you simply draw two lines connecting opposite corners and locate where they cross.
Each line drawn between opposite vertices in those four-sided shapes is a ___________, and their ___________ marks the exact middle of the shape.
A diamond-shaped ___________ also shares this half-turn property, with its crossing lines meeting at a right angle.
A six-sided ___________, like a honeycomb cell, has three main diagonals meeting at one central point, allowing it to overlap itself after a 180° rotation.
Unlike the shapes above, an ___________ does not have a center of symmetry. If you rotate a three-sided warning sign half a turn, it points in the opposite direction instead of overlapping itself.
